sentences.text: Solicitor Daniel Hughes attended the meeting with client Chloe Mason.
The purpose of the meeting was to discuss the council's letter before proceedings and the meeting scheduled for December 1st.
Chloe Mason is the client, and she provided a detailed account of events involving her children, Alfie and Poppy, and her partner Jordan.
Poppy is 14 months old and is walking everywhere.
Alfie attends Little Stars nursery on Bank Street, Monday to Friday, mornings.
Alfie is a fussy eater and only eats pasta and fish fingers.
Alfie sleeps from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m.
The council's letter cites concerns about a bruise on Alfie's arm seen by nursery on November 9th and police being called to the house in October.
Chloe told social worker Ms Okoye that Alfie fell off the sofa.
Chloe stated that Jordan slapped Alfie across the face because he wouldn't eat his tea.
The incident where Jordan slapped Alfie occurred on Sunday, November 8th, around 5 o'clock.
The bruise on Alfie's arm came from Jordan grabbing him by the arm and pulling him off a chair.
Chloe was at the sink when she saw the bruise on Alfie's arm.
Jordan told Chloe to say that Alfie fell off the sofa when the social worker Ms Okoye came to the house.
Police were called in October after a neighbour rang them following an argument and shouting between Chloe and Jordan.
Jordan is currently at his mum's and will return on Saturday.
Chloe wants her children to stay with her and expressed a desire to keep Alfie and Poppy with her.
Jordan claims he will take the children if Chloe leaves him, specifically saying he will take Poppy because she is his.
Jordan has not taken the children anywhere without Chloe's agreement, though he has made such claims during arguments.
Chloe receives Universal Credit and child benefit for both children, and Jordan has the joint bank card.
Chloe has not previously known that her Universal Credit can be paid into her own account.
Chloe's mother has been helping with food this week.
Solicitor Daniel Hughes advised that Chloe should tell social worker Ms Okoye the truth about the incident with Jordan and the bruise, before the December 1st meeting.
Solicitor Daniel Hughes advised that if Chloe leaves Jordan, he cannot take the children without going to court, and a court would hear about the incident with Alfie.
Solicitor Daniel Hughes advised that Chloe can apply for a non-molestation order to stop Jordan from coming to the house.
Solicitor Daniel Hughes advised that Chloe is likely to receive legal aid for the non-molestation order application.
Solicitor Daniel Hughes advised that a mother who tells the truth and acts to keep her child safe is in a stronger position than one who supports her partner's story.
Chloe gave permission for the solicitor to write to social worker Ms Okoye with the information provided during the meeting.
The solicitor will write to Ms Okoye by Thursday, December 26th, with Chloe's account details and send a copy to Chloe.
Chloe will speak to Harbridge Women's Aid today to discuss a safety plan for when Jordan returns on Saturday.
